description: Phase 1 Foundation — CLAUDE.md rewrite, dependency upgrades, database cleanup, session persistence, terminal profiles, command palette, quick commands, and design system tokens

Upgrade @xterm/xterm and ALL @xterm/addon-* packages to latest (6.x for core, matching versions for addons)

Upgrade vite and typescript to latest

userStories.title: Database cleanup migration — drop legacy tables
userStories.description: As a developer, I want unused database tables from the old job system removed so the schema only contains tables relevant to the terminal-first architecture.
acceptanceCriteria: Create migration `database/migrations/019_cleanup_and_quick_commands.sql`

DROP IF EXISTS all legacy tables: step_execution_results, server_job_results, job_runs, job_schedules, job_template_steps, job_templates, command_templates, job_types, notification_policy_channels, notification_policies, notification_channels, notification_log, webhooks, task_history, metrics, tags, server_tags, job_catalog, job_catalog_categories, job_catalog_favorites, server_capabilities
ALTER TABLE terminal_profiles ADD COLUMN user_id INTEGER REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
UPDATE terminal_profiles layout values: '1'->'single', '2h'->'split-h', '2v'->'split-v', '4'->'quad'
CREATE TABLE quick_commands with columns: id, user_id, name, command, server_id (nullable FK to servers), category, sort_order, created_at, updated_at
Add indexes: idx_quick_commands_user, idx_quick_commands_server
`cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` passes
`cargo test --workspace` passes
userStories.notes: Check migration files in database/migrations/ — 018 is the latest, so this is 019. Use DROP TABLE IF EXISTS for safety. The quick_commands table replaces the quick_commands TEXT field on terminal_profiles (which stored a flat Vec<String> — too limited). Leave the old column on terminal_profiles (SQLite DROP COLUMN compatibility). Tables to preserve: servers, credentials, users, settings, terminal_profiles, server_host_keys. Verify migration runs by checking `cargo test --workspace` which runs migrations on in-memory SQLite.

userStories.title: Session serialize/restore with reconnect prompt
userStories.description: As a user, I want my terminal scrollback to survive page refreshes and disconnections, with a clear reconnect prompt when a PTY session is lost.
acceptanceCriteria: Import and load @xterm/addon-serialize in TerminalPane.svelte alongside existing addons
Add serializeBuffer() function that saves terminal buffer to sessionStorage keyed by tab ID with 512KB size limit
Call serializeBuffer() on: disconnect(), document visibilitychange (when hidden), and beforeunload events
Add restoreBuffer() function that writes saved buffer to terminal before WebSocket connect
Call restoreBuffer() at the start of connect() before opening the WebSocket
Remove saved buffer from sessionStorage when user explicitly closes a tab

When a PTY session drops unexpectedly, show a reconnect prompt overlay on the terminal: 'Session disconnected. [Reconnect] [New Session]' — implement as a small overlay div positioned over the terminal pane
For size limit: if serialized data exceeds 512KB, reduce terminal scrollback option temporarily, serialize, then restore original scrollback value
Add visibilitychange and beforeunload listeners with proper cleanup in onMount return function
`cd ui && npm run check` passes
`cd ui && npm run build` passes
userStories.notes: File: ui/src/lib/components/terminal/TerminalPane.svelte. The serialize addon API: `const data = serializeAddon.serialize()` returns a string, `terminal.write(data)` restores it. Storage key: `svrctlrs-term-buffer-${tabId}` where tabId comes from the component's props. The reconnect prompt is display-only — the serialized buffer shows what was on screen but the shell session cannot be resumed (PTY is stateless from the client side). The overlay should have two buttons: 'Reconnect' (calls connect()) and 'New Session' (calls disconnect then connect with fresh state). Use $effect for the visibilitychange listener with cleanup.

acceptanceCriteria: Add CSS tokens to app.css @theme block: --density (1), --duration-fast (100ms), --duration-normal (200ms), --duration-slow (300ms), --easing-default

userStories.notes: Read ui/src/app.css for the existing @theme block structure — add the new tokens inside it. For the density scaling, start simple: just define the CSS variables and the compact override. Actual component padding adjustments can be incremental. In +layout.svelte, use a reactive effect: `$effect(() => { document.documentElement.dataset.density = isMobile() ? 'compact' : 'comfortable'; })`. Import isMobile from '$lib/state/mobile.svelte.js'. The /simplify skill reviews recently changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency — run it after all other changes are committed.
